messages.subject: Re: More detailed output request please ...
messages.body_plain:
Dear Kory,

1. about suggested additional columns : I think that your suggested additional information is the preliminary summary about data. So, It can be summarized and reported in dataProcess step, not in group comparison result. Especially, 1) SD for one group is not calculated in group comparison step, SE is calculated with linear model considering multiple groups 2) and group comparison can be performed with linear combination of multiple groups. So, hard to generalized reference group, test group. Currently, we can have some information. (However, it will be before imputation and TMP summarization. Just summary of log2(normalized) intensities.) 'ConditionPlot' after dataProcess function uses some of this information and you can get output in dataProcessPlot step. For example,

quant <- dataProcess(SRMRawData)
dataProcessPlots(quant, type='ConditionPlot', save_condition_plot_result = TRUE)

then, 'ConditionPlot_value.csv' file will be generated. It will be like below.

Protein Condition Mean SD numMeasurement 95% CI
IDHC 1 6.432392385 0.742369314 3 1.364019156
IDHC 2 6.439553948 0.135767168 3 0.249456724
IDHC 3 6.591767688 0.44685468 3 0.821044637
IDHC 4 6.759387656 0.569713763 3 1.046784224
IDHC 5 6.980621513 0.440780922 3 0.809884797

We will think about reporting more additional information. Thank you for your suggesting.

2. MSstats used xxx$RunlevelData for group comparison,( lm or lmer ), which is run-level summarized data after imputation and TMP.

3. if you want to see embedded function, check methods.R

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena

messages.subject_clean: Handling of shared (non-unique) peptides by dataProcess
messages.body_plain:
Dear Juan,

If you used 'MQtoMSstatsFormat' function to convert MaxQuant output to MSstats input format, unique peptides will be removed with default option.

If you use other tool, MSstats assumes that 'PeptideSequence' or 'PeptideModifiedSequence' column has unique peptide. So, certain PeptideSequence measured for more than 1 protein, MSstats will generate error message with list of these peptides, as duplicated rows.

So, If you have non-unique peptides, I recommend to remove before using MSstats.

Hope to help.

- Meena

messages.subject: Phosphoproteomics Time Course
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I'd like to try MSstats (in R environment) for timecourse consisting of 16 time points and it is phosphoproteomics (so I'm interested in quantifying phosphopeptides rather than proteins, no protein inference is required). I just want your advice guys if MSstats can be useful for my experimental design (before digging into the manuals).
OK, Let's start.
It might sound weird but I'm not interested in defining phosphopeptides with significant changes (I will do it myself based on the shape of the kinetic profile). What I need is correction for a systematic variability between measurements (=time points), in my setup only small (~10-15%) proportion of phopshopeptides will change their abundance so I assume that median of the log2(Intensities) for all detected peptides can be used for normalization.
I'm going to use MaxQuant for pSites ID , but I can use evidence.txt instead of phosphoSTYsites.txt output (I can aggregate phosphopeptides containing same pSites later manually).
I will have only one replicate (becase significance will be defined based on the profile shape and it will be based on 16 measurements, so I doubt that I can get consistent temporal profile just by chance)
I will not use 2DLC fractionation, so 1 raw file - 1 time point.
Annotation.csv will look like: Condition = "WT" / BioReplicate = "1" / Experiment = "T00, T01, ..., T15" / Raw.file = just names of my raw files

So, cam MSstats help me here? I need only normalization for technical variability across samples (time points). BTW if this normalization will be based only on shifting log(intensity) distributions to the common median value I can do it myself.

Also it would be nice to have at least one simple tutorial, in the pdf manual you have only the description for available functions and I'm not really sure what would be their correct order of execution.
Thanks in advance for your help,
Evgeny.

messages.subject: Re: Phosphoproteomics Time Course
messages.body_plain:
Dear Eugene,

the 'protein' column does not have to have an actual protein id. It is only used to group features that should be combined for quantification. So if in this column you give unique ids to individual phosphopeptides (or phosphosites), then quantification will be performed with respect to these groups. The only restriction is that each group is denoted by a unique string of characters.

HTH
Olga

messages.subject: Re: Imputation with MBimpute
messages.body_plain:
Thank you for giving us to clarify the combination of options.

1. imputation, with model-based value
quant <- dataProcess(msstats.raw, fillIncompleteRows=TRUE, normalization="quantile")

2. imputation, not model based imputation, but just impute with minimum value per feature for NA censored value.
quant <- dataProcess(msstats.raw, fillIncompleteRows=TRUE, normalization="quantile", MBimpute=FALSE)

3. no imputation, there is no censored Intensity.
quant <- dataProcess(msstats.raw, fillIncompleteRows=TRUE, normalization="quantile", censoredInt=NULL)

all three combination will have different results.
If you don't want any imputation, please use option 3.

Hope to help.

-Meena
